text:
leo: Quick heads-up: kythera-14b (int4) canary showed repeat warmstart OOMs when users hit long chat histories. Repro on canary-3 with batch_concurrency=3 and max_new_tokens=512.

anya: got logs?

leo: snippet:
``nCUDA OOM allocating 1.05GiB for kv_prefetch buffer
 at serving/kv_prefetch.cpp:256
```

hakeem: smells like fragmentation + prefetch. quick mitigation: set runtime.prefetch.enabled=false and reduce generation.max_new_tokens to 200.

leo: tried that. OOMs dropped but p95 latency rose ~60ms. Throughput down ~18%.

anya: other knobs to try: increase slot_compactor_reserve to 0.05, lower kv_trim_threshold to 0.5, and reduce batch_concurrency to 1 or 2.

hakeem: also test kernel affinity tweak: runtime.kernel_affinity=prefer-small-alloc — helped another int4 model.

ci-bot: queued microbench (warm-kv) and 1k eval comparing fp16/int8/int4 — results ETA 45m.

sarah: note on quality: last int4 run we saw ROUGE-L dip ~-0.8 on long summaries. If mem fixes cost too much perf, prefer int8 for GA.

leo: agreed. plan: (1) run bench + eval (ci-bot), (2) try slot_compactor_reserve=0.05 + prefetch off + max_new_tokens=200 on canary, (3) if int4 OOM_rate >0.5% or ROUGE-L <-1.0, switch GA default to int8.

anya: logging peak_gpu_mem per warm request in bench. will attach graphs.

ci-bot: microbench results: int4 peak_warm=12.7GiB, int8 peak_warm=11.0GiB, OOM_rate int4=1.2% -> with overrides 0.4%.

leo: overrides look promising. opening PR to set conservative model_overrides and document default max_new_tokens=200 for kythera until int4 frag fixes landed.

sarah: thanks. keep int4 as experimental route-level variant for now.
